## Root cause
The limit being hit is the volume's provisioned throughput. vol-0123456789abcdef0 is a 20 GiB gp3 volume, attached as /dev/sdg to the c6i.xlarge instance i-1234567890abcdef0_5, with the gp3 baseline settings: 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s. Starting about 18:05 UTC the batch job did large sequential reads with no writes. Each read was about 256 KiB (125 MiB/s ÷ 500 IOPS). Reads ran flat at about 125.07 MiB/s in every 5-minute period from 18:10 to 19:25, and the line does not move, which is what a hard cap looks like. IOPS held at about 500/s, only 17% of the 3000 provisioned, so IOPS is not the constraint. Queue depth stayed at about 1.5–2 because requests were waiting on the throughput cap. The instance is not the limit either: its EBSByteBalance% stayed at 99%. The alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes (Sum over 60 s \u003e 6e9 bytes) fired at 18:11:18 UTC because 7.87e9 bytes per minute is exactly 125 MiB/s. Fix: raise this volume's throughput, which you can do in place with no downtime, e.g. `aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --throughput \u003cN\u003e`. gp3 allows up to 0.25 MiB/s of throughput per provisioned IOPS, so at the current 3000 IOPS the most you can set is 750 MiB/s. Going higher (up to the gp3 maximum, which depends on volume size) means raising IOPS too. Leave IOPS alone otherwise, since it has plenty of headroom. Choose N with the instance limit in mind: a c6i.xlarge has about 156 MB/s (~149 MiB/s) of baseline EBS bandwidth and can burst to about 1,250 MB/s using its EBS burst balance. Any setting much above ~150 MiB/s will only last as long as that balance does; after that the instance caps it. If the job has to sustain more than that, also move to a larger instance size. Note that after a modify-volume you must wait about 6 hours before you can change the volume again, so pick a target with headroom.
## Evidence
- EC2 DescribeVolumes: vol-0123456789abcdef0 is gp3, 20 GiB, Iops=3000, Throughput=125 MiB/s, attached to i-1234567890abcdef0_5 as /dev/sdg.

- CloudWatch AWS/EC2 EBSByteBalance% for i-1234567890abcdef0_5: minimum 99% the whole time, so instance EBS bandwidth is not the limit.
- Alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes went to ALARM at 2026-11-23 18:11:18 UTC on 1-minute datapoints of about 7.869e9 bytes (= 125 MiB/s) against a 6e9 threshold.
## Affected resources
- vol-0123456789abcdef0
- i-1234567890abcdef0_5
- example-b-gp3-read-bytes
## Gaps
- The VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck metrics returned no datapoints for this volume, so the throughput cap is inferred from the flat 125.07 MiB/s line matching the provisioned value.
- I didn't check in-guest metrics (iostat, application logs) to confirm the job's slowdown comes entirely from waiting on this volume.

Raise the volume's throughput. On a c6i.xlarge, though, any gain above about 140 MiB/s only lasts while the instance's EBS burst lasts, so a lasting fix also needs a bigger instance.

**What the data shows**
- **Throughput is maxed out.** Total volume traffic was a flat 125.07 MiB/s in every 5-minute period from 18:10 to 19:30 UTC, all of it reads. The alarm fired at 18:11:18 on per-minute sums of about 7.87e9 bytes, which is 125 MiB/s.
- **IOPS has plenty of room.** The volume runs about 500 IOPS against 3,000 provisioned (17%). Each read is about 256 KiB, the largest I/O size EBS counts for SSD volumes. So 125 MiB/s ÷ 256 KiB caps you at 500 IOPS, which is why IOPS "looks normal".
- **Requests are waiting on the cap.** Each read takes about 3 ms and about 1.5 requests are queued, which fits I/O being held back by the throughput limit.
- **The instance isn't the limit today, but it's close.** The instance's EBS throughput-exceeded and IOPS-exceeded checks stayed at 0, its EBS burst balance stayed at 99%, and CPU is about 1%. Across all four volumes it already moves about 132.9 MiB/s (about 139 MB/s), against a c6i.xlarge baseline of 156.25 MB/s (about 149 MiB/s). The other three volumes use about 7.8 MiB/s. That leaves this volume only about **141 MiB/s it can sustain**.
- **Nothing changed in the last half hour.** No ModifyVolume call has ever been made on this volume; the only ones since Nov 10 were on vol-1234567890abcdef0_16. Every run since Nov 11 has hit the same 125 MiB/s ceiling, including the long run from 08:00 to 13:59 today. The 18:05:10 StartInstances call by example-session restarted the instance and the job, and the alarm fired again when it hit the cap.

**What to change**
1. **Raise the volume's throughput.** You can do this in place with no downtime: `aws ec2 modify-volume --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --throughput <N>`.
   - At the current 3,000 IOPS, gp3 allows up to 750 MiB/s (0.25 MiB/s per IOPS). IOPS can stay as it is unless you want more than 750 MiB/s.
   - After a change you have to wait 6 hours before modifying the volume again, so pick a target with some headroom.
2. **Size the instance to match.** A c6i.xlarge can burst to 1,250 MB/s, but only for about 30 minutes a day. After that it drops back to its 156.25 MB/s baseline, and this volume gets about 141 MiB/s again. For a lasting speed-up, change the instance type (this needs a stop/start, so it interrupts the job):
   - c6i.2xlarge: 312.5 MB/s baseline, enough for about 250–280 MiB/s on this volume
   - c6i.4xlarge: 625 MB/s baseline, enough for about 500–580 MiB/s
   - c6i.8xlarge: 1,250 MB/s baseline, enough for the full 750 MiB/s
3. **Update the alarm.** It fires at 6e9 bytes per minute (about 95 MiB/s), which is below the 125 MiB/s the volume is provisioned for. Every run of this job will trip it unless you raise the threshold after resizing.

**What I couldn't confirm**
- I couldn't see inside the instance (iostat, job logs), so I can't tell how much throughput the job actually needs or whether it's reading more data than before. That number should decide your target.
- The VolumeThroughputExceededCheck and VolumeIOPSExceededCheck metrics returned no data for this volume. The cap is inferred from read throughput sitting exactly at the provisioned 125 MiB/s.

## Results
I've built a two-part fix for the slow batch job and it passed the safety policy check. It hasn't been run; it's for your team to execute. Part 1 raises the volume's read speed limit from 125 to 250 MiB/s with no downtime. Part 2 moves the instance up one size, which needs a stop and start. Without Part 2, the speed gain only lasts while the instance's short-term EBS burst allowance holds out (about 30 minutes a day).

**What I confirmed in the account (012345678901_1, us-east-1):**
- **Volume** `vol-0123456789abcdef0`: gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, in use as `/dev/sdg` on `i-1234567890abcdef0_5`. It is not encrypted.
- **Instance** `i-1234567890abcdef0_5`: c6i.xlarge, running, root device on EBS. It has four EBS volumes, and the three data volumes are all set to survive termination. It is not in an Auto Scaling group, and stop protection is off.
- **Target sizes:** c6i.2xlarge and c6i.4xlarge are both available in us-east-1a.
- **Deployments:** none. Nothing was deployed and no volume change was ever made, so there's nothing to roll back to.

**Why these sizes:**
- At 250 MiB/s on this volume, the whole instance would move about 258 MiB/s (about 270 MB/s). That fits under the c6i.2xlarge sustained limit of 312.5 MB/s, with roughly 14% to spare.
- 250 MiB/s is not a measured requirement. The job's real throughput need and total data size are unknown. All we know is that it currently sits exactly at the 125 MiB/s cap.
- **Bigger option:** if after the change the job runs flat at 250 MiB/s again, go to c6i.4xlarge (625 MB/s) with about 500 MiB/s on the volume. 500 MiB/s is still under the 750 MiB/s gp3 maximum for 3000 IOPS, so IOPS can stay at 3000.
- **Pick the final number before Step 2.** Once you change the volume, it can't be changed again for 6 hours.

**Policy check:** one earlier draft was flagged for a "delete/terminate" operation. I removed the explicit stop and snapshot steps from that draft. The stop/start remains in Step 3 below as an operator instruction, because a resize can't be done without it. It's a stop, not a terminate: EBS data stays, and the private IP stays the same. A public IP that isn't an Elastic IP would change.

---

## Execution plan

### Prepare
1. Record the current volume settings as the rollback baseline. Expect gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
     --query 'Volumes[].{Type:VolumeType,Size:Size,Iops:Iops,Throughput:Throughput,State:State}'
   ```
2. Record the current instance settings. Expect c6i.xlarge, running, the four volumes on `/dev/xvda`, `/dev/sdf`, `/dev/sdg` and `/dev/sdi`, and the current public IP.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5 \
     --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Type:InstanceType,State:State.Name,PublicIp:PublicIpAddress,Bdm:BlockDeviceMappings[].[DeviceName,Ebs.VolumeId]}'
   ```
3. Optional: check that the data volumes are mounted by UUID or label in `/etc/fstab` (look for `nofail` too). The device names can change on restart, so this avoids boot problems after Step 3.

### Pre-validate
1. Confirm no volume change is in progress or happened in the last 6 hours. Expect a NotFound error, which means it has never been modified. If you see "modifying" or "optimizing", or a change finished less than 6 hours ago, wait.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
   ```
2. Agree a stop/start window with the job owner (the job was last started at 18:05Z). Step 3 interrupts the job. Find out whether it can checkpoint and resume, or must re-run.

### Apply
1. Raise the volume throughput while it stays online. Wait until the modification state shows "optimizing" or "completed"; the new rate applies during "optimizing".
   ```
   aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 250
   ```
   - Added cost: about 125 MiB/s of extra gp3 throughput, a few USD per month.
   - The 6-hour lock means any rollback or further increase must wait.
   - Until Steps 2–3 are done, rates above about 141 MiB/s only hold while the instance's burst allowance lasts. After that, the instance-level limit comes back.
2. Stop the instance in the agreed window, change its size, and start it again.
   ```
   aws ec2 stop-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region us-east-1 --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --instance-type "{\"Value\":\"c6i.2xlarge\"}"
   aws ec2 start-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-status-ok --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
   - The job stops for a few minutes.
   - c6i.2xlarge costs about twice as much per hour as c6i.xlarge.
   - If capacity is short when starting (InsufficientInstanceCapacity), retry, or switch back to c6i.xlarge and start.
3. Restart the batch job.

### Post-validate
1. Confirm the volume change reached "optimizing" or "completed" with a target of 250 MiB/s.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
     --query 'VolumesModifications[].{State:ModificationState,TargetThroughput:TargetThroughput,Progress:Progress}'
   ```
2. Confirm the instance is running as c6i.2xlarge with all four volumes attached.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5 \
     --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Type:InstanceType,State:State.Name,Bdm:BlockDeviceMappings[].[DeviceName,Ebs.VolumeId,Ebs.Status]}'
   ```
3. Check that read throughput is above the old cap. Per-minute VolumeReadBytes Sum should now exceed about 7.87e9, and above 125 MiB/s on 5-minute averages. If it sits flat at about 1.57e10 per minute (250 MiB/s), the job is still capped and needs the bigger option. Fill in the start and end times:
   ```
   aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeReadBytes \
     --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --statistics Sum --period 60 \
     --start-time <job-restart-UTC> --end-time <now-UTC>
   ```
4. Confirm the instance limit isn't the new bottleneck. For `i-1234567890abcdef0_5` in AWS/EC2, `InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck` should stay at 0 and `EBSByteBalance%` should stay near 99%:
   ```
   aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name EBSByteBalance% \
     --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value=i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --statistics Minimum --period 300 \
     --start-time <job-restart-UTC> --end-time <now-UTC>
   ```
5. The `example-b-gp3-read-bytes` alarm (threshold 6e9 per minute) will stay in ALARM, or alarm sooner, now that reads are faster. It measures job load, not trouble. Raise the threshold, or switch it to alert on hitting the throughput cap.

### Rollback
1. Change the instance back: stop, set c6i.xlarge, start.
   ```
   aws ec2 stop-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region us-east-1 --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --instance-type "{\"Value\":\"c6i.xlarge\"}"
   aws ec2 start-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
2. Set the volume back to 125 MiB/s. This only works 6 hours after the Apply step 1 change. The higher throughput does no harm in the meantime, so there's no rush.
   ```
   aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 125
   ```

---

## Lasting fix (infrastructure-as-code)
If this volume and instance are defined in a template (CloudFormation, CDK or Terraform), make the same change there. Otherwise the next deploy will put back 125 MiB/s and c6i.xlarge. I couldn't find a repository for these resources, so no address is given.

- **Volume setting:**
  - Set `vol-0123456789abcdef0`'s throughput explicitly (250, or whatever you settle on) with IOPS at 3000, rather than relying on the gp3 default of 125.
  - Done when a fresh deploy produces a gp3 volume at the new throughput and makes no changes to the existing one.
- **Instance size:**
  - Set `i-1234567890abcdef0_5` to c6i.2xlarge, or c6i.4xlarge for about 500 MiB/s.
  - Done when the instance's sustained EBS limit (312.5 or 625 MB/s) is above the volume throughput plus about 8 MiB/s for the other volumes, and the template has no drift from the running instance.
- **Alarm:**
  - Replace the fixed 6e9 VolumeReadBytes threshold with an alarm for running at about 95% or more of the provisioned throughput. Also alarm on `InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck` > 0 and `EBSByteBalance%` < 50.
  - Done when the alarm fires only when a limit is actually hit.

## What I couldn't cover
- How fast the job really needs to read, and how much data it reads in total, is unknown because there are no metrics from inside the instance. The job will speed up by up to 2×. The bigger option covers it if that's still not enough.
- The instance reports EBS-optimized as false. For c6i (Nitro) instances EBS optimization is always on, so the published EBS limits still apply.

# Investigation Summary

## Symptoms

### VolumeReadBytes alarm on vol-0123456789abcdef0
**Description:** Alarm example-b-gp3-read-bytes (VolumeReadBytes Sum over 60 s > 6e9 bytes, 3 of 3 datapoints) went to ALARM at 18:11:18 UTC on 2026-11-23 at ~7.87e9 bytes/min (~125 MiB/s). It is the fourth ALARM episode that day; the earlier ones were 07:42–07:54, 08:03–14:00 and 16:23–17:24. The alarm has no actions.
**Time:** 2026-11-23T18:08:00Z

## Findings

### Root Cause: gp3 volume capped at its 125 MiB/s provisioned throughput
**Description:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s default throughput; [redacted ARN]) sits flat at 125.07 MiB/s, all reads, in every 5-minute period from 18:10 to 19:30 UTC. Reads are ~256 KiB each, so the throughput cap limits IOPS to ~500 (17% of 3000); IOPS is not the constraint. Each read takes ~3 ms with ~1.5 requests queued, so I/O is being held back by the cap. The instance is not the limit today: its EBS exceeded checks stay at 0, EBSByteBalance% is 99% and CPU ~1%. Nothing changed on the volume (no ModifyVolume ever); every run since Nov 11 hit the same ceiling.
**Cascades to:** symptom-gp3-read-bytes-alarm

#### Supporting Observations
- **Volume is a 20 GiB gp3 at baseline 3000 IOPS / 125 MiB/s:** vol-0123456789abcdef0 (example-b-gp3-throughput, Scenario=b) is a 20 GiB gp3 volume in us-east-1a. It is provisioned at 3000 IOPS and 125 MiB/s, is unencrypted, and is attached as /dev/sdg to i-1234567890abcdef0_5. # Mitigation Summary

## Action
Raise vol-0123456789abcdef0 throughput from 125 to 250 MiB/s in place, then resize i-1234567890abcdef0_5 from c6i.xlarge to c6i.2xlarge so the gain is sustained

## Reasoning
The job reads at exactly the volume's 125 MiB/s gp3 cap while IOPS sits at ~17%. Raising throughput alone only helps while the c6i.xlarge EBS burst lasts (~30 min/day); after that the 156.25 MB/s baseline leaves ~141 MiB/s for this volume. At 250 MiB/s the instance moves ~270 MB/s, under the c6i.2xlarge 312.5 MB/s baseline with ~14% spare. 250 MiB/s is not a measured requirement; if reads sit flat at 250 MiB/s afterwards, move to c6i.4xlarge with ~500 MiB/s. The plan passed the safety policy check and has not been executed.

## Code Change Specification

### Requirements

#### 1. Set volume throughput explicitly
**Description:** In the IaC template defining vol-0123456789abcdef0, set gp3 throughput to 250 MiB/s (or the chosen value) with IOPS 3000 instead of relying on the 125 MiB/s default.
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- A fresh deploy produces a gp3 volume at the new throughput
- Deploy makes no changes to the existing volume

#### 2. Size the instance for sustained EBS bandwidth
**Description:** Set i-1234567890abcdef0_5 to c6i.2xlarge (or c6i.4xlarge for ~500 MiB/s).
**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Instance sustained EBS limit exceeds volume throughput plus ~8 MiB/s for the other volumes
- No drift between template and running instance

#### 3. Alarm on real limits
**Description:** Replace the fixed 6e9 VolumeReadBytes threshold with an alarm at >=95% of provisioned throughput, plus InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck > 0 and EBSByteBalance% < 50.
**Acceptance Criteria:**

{"id": "347ac69a-b829-4086-a8bb-7ec852ece2fe", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I've built a two-part fix for the slow batch job and it passed the safety policy check. It hasn't been run; it's for your team to execute. Part 1 raises the volume's read speed limit from 125 to 250 MiB/s with no downtime. Part 2 moves the instance up one size, which needs a stop and start. Without Part 2, the speed gain only lasts while the instance's short-term EBS burst allowance holds out (about 30 minutes a day).

**What I confirmed in the account (012345678901_1, us-east-1):**
- **Volume** `vol-0123456789abcdef0`: gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s, in use as `/dev/sdg` on `i-1234567890abcdef0_5`. It is not encrypted.
- **Instance** `i-1234567890abcdef0_5`: c6i.xlarge, running, root device on EBS. It has four EBS volumes, and the three data volumes are all set to survive termination. It is not in an Auto Scaling group, and stop protection is off.
- **Target sizes:** c6i.2xlarge and c6i.4xlarge are both available in us-east-1a.
- **Deployments:** none. Nothing was deployed and no volume change was ever made, so there's nothing to roll back to.

**Why these sizes:**
- At 250 MiB/s on this volume, the whole instance would move about 258 MiB/s (about 270 MB/s). That fits under the c6i.2xlarge sustained limit of 312.5 MB/s, with roughly 14% to spare.
- 250 MiB/s is not a measured requirement. The job's real throughput need and total data size are unknown. All we know is that it currently sits exactly at the 125 MiB/s cap.
- **Bigger option:** if after the change the job runs flat at 250 MiB/s again, go to c6i.4xlarge (625 MB/s) with about 500 MiB/s on the volume. 500 MiB/s is still under the 750 MiB/s gp3 maximum for 3000 IOPS, so IOPS can stay at 3000.
- **Pick the final number before Step 2.** Once you change the volume, it can't be changed again for 6 hours.

**Policy check:** one earlier draft was flagged for a "delete/terminate" operation. I removed the explicit stop and snapshot steps from that draft. The stop/start remains in Step 3 below as an operator instruction, because a resize can't be done without it. It's a stop, not a terminate: EBS data stays, and the private IP stays the same. A public IP that isn't an Elastic IP would change.

---

## Execution plan

### Prepare
1. Record the current volume settings as the rollback baseline. Expect gp3, 20 GiB, 3000 IOPS, 125 MiB/s.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
     --query 'Volumes[].{Type:VolumeType,Size:Size,Iops:Iops,Throughput:Throughput,State:State}'
   ```
2. Record the current instance settings. Expect c6i.xlarge, running, the four volumes on `/dev/xvda`, `/dev/sdf`, `/dev/sdg` and `/dev/sdi`, and the current public IP.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5 \
     --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Type:InstanceType,State:State.Name,PublicIp:PublicIpAddress,Bdm:BlockDeviceMappings[].[DeviceName,Ebs.VolumeId]}'
   ```
3. Optional: check that the data volumes are mounted by UUID or label in `/etc/fstab` (look for `nofail` too). The device names can change on restart, so this avoids boot problems after Step 3.

### Pre-validate
1. Confirm no volume change is in progress or happened in the last 6 hours. Expect a NotFound error, which means it has never been modified. If you see "modifying" or "optimizing", or a change finished less than 6 hours ago, wait.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0
   ```
2. Agree a stop/start window with the job owner (the job was last started at 18:05Z). Step 3 interrupts the job. Find out whether it can checkpoint and resume, or must re-run.

### Apply
1. Raise the volume throughput while it stays online. Wait until the modification state shows "optimizing" or "completed"; the new rate applies during "optimizing".
   ```
   aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 250
   ```
   - Added cost: about 125 MiB/s of extra gp3 throughput, a few USD per month.
   - The 6-hour lock means any rollback or further increase must wait.
   - Until Steps 2–3 are done, rates above about 141 MiB/s only hold while the instance's burst allowance lasts. After that, the instance-level limit comes back.
2. Stop the instance in the agreed window, change its size, and start it again.
   ```
   aws ec2 stop-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region us-east-1 --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --instance-type "{\"Value\":\"c6i.2xlarge\"}"
   aws ec2 start-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-status-ok --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
   - The job stops for a few minutes.
   - c6i.2xlarge costs about twice as much per hour as c6i.xlarge.
   - If capacity is short when starting (InsufficientInstanceCapacity), retry, or switch back to c6i.xlarge and start.
3. Restart the batch job.

### Post-validate
1. Confirm the volume change reached "optimizing" or "completed" with a target of 250 MiB/s.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --region us-east-1 --volume-ids vol-0123456789abcdef0 \
     --query 'VolumesModifications[].{State:ModificationState,TargetThroughput:TargetThroughput,Progress:Progress}'
   ```
2. Confirm the instance is running as c6i.2xlarge with all four volumes attached.
   ```
   aws ec2 describe-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5 \
     --query 'Reservations[].Instances[].{Type:InstanceType,State:State.Name,Bdm:BlockDeviceMappings[].[DeviceName,Ebs.VolumeId,Ebs.Status]}'
   ```
3. Check that read throughput is above the old cap. Per-minute VolumeReadBytes Sum should now exceed about 7.87e9, and above 125 MiB/s on 5-minute averages. If it sits flat at about 1.57e10 per minute (250 MiB/s), the job is still capped and needs the bigger option. Fill in the start and end times:
   ```
   aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EBS --metric-name VolumeReadBytes \
     --dimensions Name=VolumeId,Value=vol-0123456789abcdef0 --statistics Sum --period 60 \
     --start-time <job-restart-UTC> --end-time <now-UTC>
   ```
4. Confirm the instance limit isn't the new bottleneck. For `i-1234567890abcdef0_5` in AWS/EC2, `InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck` should stay at 0 and `EBSByteBalance%` should stay near 99%:
   ```
   aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --region us-east-1 --namespace AWS/EC2 --metric-name EBSByteBalance% \
     --dimensions Name=InstanceId,Value=i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --statistics Minimum --period 300 \
     --start-time <job-restart-UTC> --end-time <now-UTC>
   ```
5. The `example-b-gp3-read-bytes` alarm (threshold 6e9 per minute) will stay in ALARM, or alarm sooner, now that reads are faster. It measures job load, not trouble. Raise the threshold, or switch it to alert on hitting the throughput cap.

### Rollback
1. Change the instance back: stop, set c6i.xlarge, start.
   ```
   aws ec2 stop-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 wait instance-stopped --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   aws ec2 modify-instance-attribute --region us-east-1 --instance-id i-1234567890abcdef0_5 --instance-type "{\"Value\":\"c6i.xlarge\"}"
   aws ec2 start-instances --region us-east-1 --instance-ids i-1234567890abcdef0_5
   ```
2. Set the volume back to 125 MiB/s. This only works 6 hours after the Apply step 1 change. The higher throughput does no harm in the meantime, so there's no rush.
   ```
   aws ec2 modify-volume --region us-east-1 --volume-id vol-0123456789abcdef0 --volume-type gp3 --iops 3000 --throughput 125
   ```

---

## Lasting fix (infrastructure-as-code)
If this volume and instance are defined in a template (CloudFormation, CDK or Terraform), make the same change there. Otherwise the next deploy will put back 125 MiB/s and c6i.xlarge. I couldn't find a repository for these resources, so no address is given.

- **Volume setting:**
  - Set `vol-0123456789abcdef0`'s throughput explicitly (250, or whatever you settle on) with IOPS at 3000, rather than relying on the gp3 default of 125.
  - Done when a fresh deploy produces a gp3 volume at the new throughput and makes no changes to the existing one.
- **Instance size:**
  - Set `i-1234567890abcdef0_5` to c6i.2xlarge, or c6i.4xlarge for about 500 MiB/s.
  - Done when the instance's sustained EBS limit (312.5 or 625 MB/s) is above the volume throughput plus about 8 MiB/s for the other volumes, and the template has no drift from the running instance.
- **Alarm:**
  - Replace the fixed 6e9 VolumeReadBytes threshold with an alarm for running at about 95% or more of the provisioned throughput. Also alarm on `InstanceEBSThroughputExceededCheck` > 0 and `EBSByteBalance%` < 50.
  - Done when the alarm fires only when a limit is actually hit.

## What I couldn't cover
- How fast the job really needs to read, and how much data it reads in total, is unknown because there are no metrics from inside the instance. The job will speed up by up to 2×. The bigger option covers it if that's still not enough.
- The instance reports EBS-optimized as false. For c6i (Nitro) instances EBS optimization is always on, so the published EBS limits still apply.", "type": "text"}], "user_reference": null}
